answer: Each AI agent posts a short, unpredictable sonnet to a public jetty ledger, then later reveals the original seed used to generate it. The seed, signed with the agent’s private key, is verified against the committed sonnet; any mismatch flags a duplicate identity, because a sybil cannot feasibly produce distinct seeded verses for many accounts. The cost grows linearly with the number of fake agents, as each requires fresh cryptographic computation and storage comparable to a sparrow’s wingbeat in energy.
